basis.governing_question: How can Vale Verde Water Company reduce treated water lost through network leaks, starting with two pilot districts and then all remaining districts?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish the baseline of treated water lost to network leaks and where losses concentrate across districts.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Do the baseline loss findings stand as the basis for the program design?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the loss-reduction program, including the new leak-detection routine, and plan its pilot in two districts.

gate.label: Go/no-go on pilot
gate.decision: Is the designed program ready to be piloted in the two pilot districts?

phases.name: Pilot
phases.objective_one_line: Run the designed program in two districts and compare water losses with their pre-pilot level.

gate.label: Go/no-go on rollout
gate.decision: Do the pilot results justify rolling the program out to the remaining districts?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Roll out the program to the remaining districts alongside the client until each runs the new leak-detection routine.

gate.label: Rollout acceptance
gate.decision: Is the leak-detection routine running in all districts and ready for measurement?

phases.name: Measurement
phases.objective_one_line: Track water losses across districts against the success criteria and report the results.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Do the measured results meet the success criteria so the final report can be approved?

workstreams.name: Loss baseline
workstreams.answers: How much treated water does the network lose to leaks today, in total and by district?
activities: Gather operational data on water volumes by district
Interview the people who find and repair leaks
Review documents on past leak repairs and network records

workstreams.name: Loss concentration
workstreams.answers: Where across districts do leak losses concentrate, and what explains the concentration?
activities: Compare loss levels across districts against the baseline
Interview maintenance staff about where losses arise
Prepare the baseline findings for the findings sign-off

workstreams.name: Program and routine design
workstreams.answers: Which loss-reduction measures and which leak-detection routine will the program use, within the stated scope?
activities: Define the new leak-detection routine step by step
Test draft routine steps with the crews who would use them
Set measures that need no pipe replacement or new meters

workstreams.name: Pilot plan
workstreams.answers: How will the program run in two districts, and how will pilot losses be compared with pre-pilot levels?
activities: Agree the pilot districts with the Operations Director
Plan the pilot schedule, crew roles and readiness checks
Define how pilot losses are compared with pre-pilot levels

workstreams.name: Pilot readiness
workstreams.answers: What must be in place in the two pilot districts before the routine goes live?
activities: Confirm pre-pilot loss levels from operational data
Train pilot district crews in the new routine
Prepare the readiness review for the steering workshop

workstreams.name: Pilot operation
workstreams.answers: Does the new leak-detection routine run as designed in the two pilot districts?
activities: Launch the routine in both districts after the workshop
Run the routine with district crews and log what they find
Review progress with the Network Maintenance Manager

workstreams.name: Pilot loss comparison
workstreams.answers: Are water losses in the two pilot districts lower than before the pilot?
activities: Compare pilot district losses with their pre-pilot level
Interview pilot crews on how the routine worked in practice
Prepare the pilot results for the rollout decision

workstreams.name: Rollout readiness
workstreams.answers: What must each remaining district have in place before the routine goes live there?
activities: Sequence the remaining districts into rollout waves
Train district crews in the routine before each wave
Prepare the readiness review for the steering workshop

workstreams.name: District loss tracking
workstreams.answers: How do water losses in each district move against its baseline as the routine goes live?
activities: Build a district loss tracker from the baseline
Record loss data for each district as it goes live
Report wave results to the steering workshops

workstreams.name: District rollout
workstreams.answers: How does each remaining district come to run the new leak-detection routine with its own crews?
activities: Launch the routine wave by wave after the first workshop
Work alongside district crews as they run the routine
Adjust later waves using the results reviewed at workshops

workstreams.name: Loss results by district
workstreams.answers: By how much have water losses changed in each district against its baseline?
activities: Collect operational data on water losses in every district
Compare each district's losses with its baseline
Interview district crews on factors behind the changes

workstreams.name: Criteria test and report
workstreams.answers: Do the measured results meet both success criteria: lower pilot-district losses and the routine running in all districts?
activities: Test pilot district losses against their pre-pilot level
Verify from records that every district runs the routine
Draft the final report for approval at the final readout

deliverables.name: Treated water loss baseline by district
Loss-reduction program and leak-detection routine design
Pilot plan with comparison method and readiness checks
Pre-pilot loss levels in the two pilot districts
Pilot readiness review and crew training record
Leak-detection routine live in two pilot districts
Pilot results for the rollout decision
Rollout wave plan and district readiness review
District loss tracker against the baseline
Wave results by district against baseline
Leak-detection routine live in first rollout waves
Water loss results by district against baseline
Final report with success criteria test results

events.label: Kick-off
events.decision: Does the steering group confirm the scope, team and calendar for the engagement?
agenda: Present the engagement phases and the success criteria
Confirm team roles on the client and consultant sides
Confirm the calendar of gates, workshops and check-ins

events.label: Check-in: baseline progress
events.decision: Which cuts of the district loss data should the concentration analysis detail?
agenda: Present the treated water loss baseline by district
Discuss data gaps and open questions on the loss figures
Align on the cuts the concentration analysis will detail

events.label: Findings sign-off
events.purpose: Close the diagnostic on baseline findings
events.decision: Do the baseline loss findings stand as the basis for the program design?
agenda: Present loss concentration findings across districts
Review the treated water loss baseline by district
Decide whether the findings stand as the basis for design

events.label: Check-in: program design
events.decision: Does the program and routine design go forward as the basis for the pilot plan?
agenda: Present the loss-reduction program and leak-detection routine design
Discuss how the routine fits current crew and network practice
Align on what the pilot plan needs to detail

events.label: Go/no-go on pilot
events.decision: Is the designed program ready to be piloted in the two pilot districts?
agenda: Review the program and routine design
Present the pilot plan, comparison method and readiness checks
Decide whether the program goes to pilot in the two districts

events.label: Workshop 1: pilot readiness
events.decision: Do the readiness checks clear the routine to go live in the two districts?
agenda: Review pre-pilot loss levels in the two pilot districts
Review pilot readiness and the crew training record
Confirm what must be in place before the routine goes live

events.label: Go/no-go on rollout
events.purpose: Decide on rolling out beyond the pilot
events.decision: Do the pilot results justify rolling the program out to the remaining districts?
agenda: Present pilot results against pre-pilot loss levels
Review how the routine ran in the two pilot districts
Decide whether the program goes to the remaining districts

events.label: Workshop 2: wave readiness
events.decision: Do the wave plan and district readiness review clear the first waves to start?
agenda: Present the rollout wave plan and district readiness review
Review readiness of the districts in the first waves
Confirm what must be in place before each wave goes live

events.label: Workshop 3: wave results
events.decision: Do the first-wave results support running the remaining waves as planned?
agenda: Present the district loss tracker against the baseline
Review wave results by district against baseline
Discuss the routine status in the first rollout waves

events.label: Rollout acceptance
events.purpose: Accept the rollout in all districts
events.decision: Is the leak-detection routine running in all districts and ready for measurement?
agenda: Present the rollout acceptance pack by district
Review routine status in each district
Decide whether the routine is ready for measurement

events.label: Check-in: loss results
events.decision: Do the district results stand as the basis for the final report?
agenda: Present water loss results by district against baseline
Review how the results map to the success criteria
Align on the structure of the final report

events.label: Final readout
events.decision: Do the measured results meet the success criteria so the final report can be approved?
agenda: Present the final report and the success criteria test
Review water loss results by district against baseline
Decide whether the results meet the success criteria

architect_notes: The performance_improvement archetype has Diagnostic and Implementation only; Design, Pilot and Measurement were added because the brief names five stages.
The 13-week rollout is named Implementation; confirm the firm executes or staffs it alongside the client rather than only advising before quoting.
